filename: Contrasting Parametric Sensitivities in Two Global Vegetation Models Using Parameter Perturbation Ensembles.pdf
title: Contrasting Parametric Sensitivities in Two Global Vegetation Models Using Parameter Perturbation Ensembles
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
code_availability: Model code is CTSM tag ctsm5.3.031 (https://github.com/ESCOMP/CTSM/tree/release-clm5.0.31) and FATES tag sci.1.82.0_api.38.0.0 (https://github.com/NGEET/fates/tree/sci.1.82.0_api.38.0.0). Ensemble generation scripts are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18285651, and figure generation scripts are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18285656.
testbed_rationale: Provides a clean, publicly archived, multi-model perturbed parameter ensemble dataset for CLM and CLM-FATES spanning 400 climatologically and ecologically representative sparse grid cells, suitable for training and validating land-surface surrogate models, emulators, and calibration routines.
pain_points: One-at-a-time (OAAT) sampling isolates single parameters and does not capture nonlinear parameter interactions or global response surfaces.
Parameter sensitivity rankings depend heavily on expert-chosen min/max physical bounds.

Structural divergences between models (e.g., LUNA dynamic Vcmax vs FATES prescribed Vcmax; differing water stress applications) mean parameter sensitivity landscapes are fundamentally non-transferable between models.
High computational burden of full global runs necessitated using a sparse-grid approximation and uniform perturbation across plant functional types.
extraction_notes: The study itself does not train machine learning models, but conducts a comprehensive perturbed parameter ensemble (PPE) sensitivity experiment designed to inform future land surface model calibration and emulation. Co-author L. R. Hawkins was funded by the NSF LEAP Science and Technology Center.
